title: C435 — Fuel tank pressure (FTP) sensor connector
introduction:
I use this page to follow the fuel tank pressure (FTP) sensor’s connection records from the connector drawing into the circuit table. The Function column separates the sensing connection, reference supply and signal return. Think of a reference as the starting edge of a ruler: the labels help explain the measurement’s connections, but they do not supply a pressure reading or prove the sensor is healthy.

Start with the identity table, match the drawing’s cavity labels to the pin rows, then read the pigtail catalog entry. This is a reading guide, not an access, fuel-plumbing, probing or replacement procedure. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention, Size and Used codes, and diagnostic limits are not defined here.

edits.why: The drawing places the cavity labels in a vertical column, with projecting housing details to the left. I use those features to navigate the illustration and match its labels to Cavity in the table. They do not establish the physical viewing side or a connector-release movement.

Keep each Cavity row intact as you read across its circuit identifier, color, gauge, function and terminal identifier. The pressure-transducer, reference-voltage and signal-return descriptions explain different circuit roles. A reference-voltage label is not a voltage specification, and a signal-return label alone does not establish a chassis-ground connection.

I use this record to relate the catalog Number to its Service Part and Engineering Shell, keeping the service item distinct from the housing identifier. The pigtail gauge and pin-table gauge describe separate records; neither supplies an approved splice or replacement-wire decision.
